# Review clarity and consistent meaning

Review terminology, reader navigation and consequential claims across project material.

[All skills](index.md) · [Collection overview](../../README.md) · [Research and inspiration](../../standards/framework-evidence.md)

## When to use it

Use when auditing existing writing or requesting a revision across related artefacts.

Example request:

> Review this task, decision and announcement for consistent meanings and explain every consequential edit.

Expected result: Located findings or an authorised revision that preserves meanings, constraints and source claims.

## A concrete example

This invented example illustrates the guidance. It is not an observed product result or a benchmark.

**Source facts and constraints:** Eligibility and coverage are distinct project concepts. Their definitions and the intended behaviour need to be established before rewriting the requirement.

The before text may obscure or overstate those facts. The revision must follow the supplied facts and constraints.

**Before**

> Improve the eligibility coverage signal across the activation surface.

**After**

> Explain what eligibility and coverage mean here, then name the behaviour that should change. Keep eligibility and coverage distinct.

Preserve the source facts, governing meanings and consequential constraints when applying the example to real work.

## Install and use

Install this skill from the versioned collection in a supported Agent Skills environment:

```sh
npx skills add https://github.com/theGeekist/skills/tree/v1.6.0 --skill review-project-language
```

Select the intended agent and installation scope when prompted. This CLI installation is separate from ChatGPT plugin registration and mobile availability. Client discovery and activation require their own verification.

Read the [complete skill instructions](../../skills/review-project-language/SKILL.md) and [bundled purpose reference](../../skills/review-project-language/references/review.md) for the full conditions and exceptions.

## Inspiration and local decisions

Microsoft, Google and the ISO plain-language public abstract inform reader-focused review. The four repository outcomes are Jason’s priorities, not an ISO certification claim.

- [Microsoft plain-word guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/style-guide/word-choice/use-simple-words-concise-sentences)
- [Google jargon guidance](https://developers.google.com/style/jargon)
- [ISO plain-language abstract](https://www.iso.org/standard/78907.html)

These sources inform selected practices; they do not certify this skill or establish better prose quality. The [source-to-guidance map](../../standards/framework-evidence.md) records what was applied, adapted or deferred.
